cells.tense: You are receiving what has not arrived yet, and the knowing is already in your hands.
cells.ask: Offer someone a possibility you have not yet decided about, and let their answer reach you.
cells.core:
You have a feel for what is coming before it gets here. That part is working. Someone can say something unfinished to you and you do not correct it, do not hurry it, do not turn your own read into the verdict. The first movement of a thing can reach you and you do not have to finish knowing it in order to be in contact with it.

The softness is keeping you in the room with people. Keep it that way. When you offer a half-formed thought instead of a finished one, what comes back tells you something you could not have reached by holding it in. That balance is worth feeding, and it is not free — it costs you the comfort of deciding everything early.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel a thing before it arrives and still stay open to it.
cells.verb: Staying open to what has not yet arrived
cells.place: In the fog with enough light for the next step

cells.tense: You are bracing for a future you have not been given yet to enter.
cells.ask: Before you answer anyone today, write down what you are afraid will happen, and let the writing be the whole act.
cells.core:
You are reaching into what has not happened and writing the ending yourself. Someone is still halfway through telling you something and you have already decided what it means — not to control them, but because the open middle is too much to stand. What might have surprised you arrives already shaped like your fear, so nothing can actually land.

The part of you that is opening is real. It is the writing ahead of it that is costing you. Give the next hour one small finished shape you can see, and let the rest of the day still be open. The open part will feel like a loss. It is the part that lets anything new reach you at all.

cells.tense: You stand at a door you already walked past and keep asking to be let in.
cells.ask: Say out loud, to one person, one thing you do not know and have not decided.
cells.core:
An old choice in you has become the air the whole thing breathes. Some opening happened once, and the way you settled after it has been deciding since — so the moving-through has stopped. The fog you know how to stand in has kept the same shape, and a shape you already expect will not reach you as anything new.

Nothing is wrong with not knowing. It is the sitting-still inside it that got frozen. Start small. Say a plainly undecided thing to someone and let them answer. The first try will feel stiff. That is fine — fresh attention is not a talent you were handed, it is something you can pick up in a single sentence.
cells.sheetLine: An old decision is standing where your open attention should be.

cells.tense: You are already open and already reading what arrives, and you call it the situation being obvious.
cells.ask: Name one thing you noticed before anyone said it, and say out loud that you are the one who noticed.
cells.core:
You are already taking in what has not yet been named — noticing the shift, the held breath, the thing someone is not saying yet. When it is working, you catch the first small change in a room and you stay with it instead of deciding it early; people feel seen by you and do not feel handled. That is happening. What is not happening is the saying-so. You talk as if the room were handing you the answer, and the answer is coming from you.

Take one thing back. Not a big confession, just a small true sentence, one you leave standing while you are around people who might have seen the same thing differently. What they say back is part of it too. Give and take belong in this, not an audience and a performance.
cells.sheetLine: You notice the room early. You just call it the room being obvious.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim I will keep out: that the person is receiving something specific from anyone, or that a particular door is closed. What a reader could say is different is the direction of the story — some people do read ambiguity as a hand held out rather than a fog, and I have to leave that open. If I am wrong about them, the asks still hold: each is a small, finished act that gains something either way. The sentence that serves me more than them is the one that would tell them what the fog means about their history.
